We specialize in guiding organizations through the complexities of disruption, enabling them to unlock value and realize sustainable growth. You'll have the opportunity to work on transformative projects that shape the future of these critical industries, collaborate with industry experts, and develop resilient strategies that respond to change and seize new opportunities. Develop project timelines, proactively identify and address resource discrepancies, to ensure timely project completion
Act as a liaison between technical teams and clients, facilitating effective communication through regular meetings and milestone reviews
Support functional teams in managing advisory and consulting initiatives focusing on domain specific product evaluation, benchmarking studies and domain specific system configurations
Monitor project deliverables across all phases, to meet established quality benchmarks and stakeholder expectations

An ability to build collaborative relationships with stakeholders through effective communication

Technical experience in GIS Technologies, ArcGIS Enterprise Solutions.
Experience in Utility domain, with understanding of Esri Utility Data Models aligned to North America standards.

Bachelor’s degree or foreign equivalent required from an accredited institution. Will also consider three years of progressive experience in the specialty in lieu of every year of education.

Medical/Dental/Vision/Life Insurance

Health and Dependent Care Reimbursement Accounts

jobs.description:
Job Description

The Division of Medical Physics in the Department of Radiation Oncology is seeking a Residency Program Coordinator 2, to manage, administer and support the operations of the Medical Physics residency program, postdoctoral scholars and visiting students. The Stanford Medical Physics residency program is accredited by the CAMPEP -- Commission on Accreditation of Medical Physics Education Programs.

The Division of Medical Physics core values are based on professionalism, integrity, and service. Our culture promotes, recognizes, and values the role of staff as partners in an environment that attracts and fosters the highest quality.

Desired Qualifications

In-depth knowledge and understanding of administrative principles and practices, as well as ability to assimilate functional operating knowledge of Stanford University.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS*:

Constantly perform desk-based computer tasks.
Frequently sitting.
Occasionally stand/walk, reach/work above shoulders, grasp lightly/fine manipulation, grasp forcefully, use a telephone, sort/file paperwork or parts, lift/carry/push/pull objects that weigh up to 10 pounds.
Rarely twist/bend/stoop/squat, kneel/crawl.
- Consistent with its obligations under the law, the University will provide reasonable accommodation to any employee with a disability who requires accommodation to perform the essential functions of his or her job.

Work Standards

Interpersonal Skills: Demonstrates the ability to work well with Stanford colleagues and clients and with external organizations.
Promote Culture of Safety: Demonstrates commitment to personal responsibility and value for safety; communicates safety concerns; uses and promotes safe behaviors based on training and lessons learned.
Subject to and expected to comply with all applicable University policies and procedures, including but not limited to the personnel policies and other policies found in the University's Administrative Guide, http://adminguide.stanford.edu .

Responsibilities

Core Duties
:

Independently implement, administer and evaluate day-to-day activities of residency/clinical fellowship program(s) by identifying and executing responsibilities, making recommendations that impact policies, programs and standards, and ensuring compliance and follow-up, as needed.
Act as key contact for the program to interpret and apply complex policies, procedures and program guidelines (such as those from ACGME – Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education). Review exceptions to policies to determine if exceptions are allowable. Identify, troubleshoot and report compliance issues and assist in correcting situations.
Initiate and manage the annual recruitment, onboarding and offboarding processes, including coordinating all interviews and collecting feedback on applicants. Summarize ratings and provide recommendations to program director and selection committee.
Participate in ranking meetings and provide feedback on strengths/suitability of applicants. Communicate requirements to newly matched residents. Administer appointments to the hospitals/university.
Manage the residency/clinical fellowship and faculty evaluation process by establishing and executing project plans, timelines, and objectives. Present analysis of programs and evaluations.
Develop, distribute, maintain and analyze the resident rotation, vacation and leave schedules based on accreditation requirements with oversight of Program Director.
Ensure compliance with accreditation, licensing board, professional association, ACGME requirements, GME Office requirements for the residency curriculum, goals and objectives for each level of training. Ensure interns are credentialed before starting any rotation.
Act as a liaison and advocate in support of residents and hospital administration. Establish relationships and act as a liaison to other hospitals, internal departments, and divisions regarding resident recruitment, orientation, annual program affiliation agreements, and external rotations. Manage the goals and objectives for fellows’ rotations through other clinics; recommend actions to be taken if goals are not being met.
May assist with budget activities for various residency activities, including monitoring expenses.
Plan annual events, organize meetings, and assist in the preparation for ACGME Site Visits and internal reviews. Develop brochures, invitations, or advertisements for events/lectures.

Minimum Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree and two years of relevant experience, or combination of education and relevant experience.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Ability to work independently and to coordinate multiple assignments with fluctuating priorities.
Excellent organizational and analytical abilities, ability to handle diverse workload.
Demonstrated good judgment in all areas of responsibility.
Agile and quick learner who can adapt easily to Stanford specific software and clinically related software.
Demonstrated ability to work well independently and take initiative while problem solving and resolving challenges.
Excellent oral and written communication skills. Ability to work with all levels of faculty and staff, and exhibit significant degree of diplomacy.
Excellent customer service skills and ability to adapt to changing work environment.
Proficient with Excel, Word and other applications required.
Ability to learn, understand and apply Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) or other subspecialties guidelines.

HETI has a great opportunity for a Senior Geologist/Senior Environmental Scientist/Senior Engineer with 10+ years’ experience in the environmental field.

This role will be responsible for providing technical and business skills and contribute to advanced solutions in the environmental, chemical, commercial, manufacturing, government, energy, financial, insurance, and/or legal sectors. This job is 100% remote.

The candidate should have experience managing consulting assignments, must work effectively in multi-disciplinary teams, is expected to be proficient in the analysis and communication of information, and must be able to work cooperatively with agencies, organizations, and individuals to guide decision-making. The successful candidate is also expected to be proficient in all facets of project management. He/she must demonstrate collaboration with colleagues throughout the organization.

Key Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Client Management & Communication:

Serve as the primary point of contact for clients and stakeholders, providing regular updates on project status and outcomes.
Collaborate with project teams, including environmental engineers, geologists, and technicians.
Communicate complex technical information to clients and stakeholders in a clear and concise manner.

Regulatory Compliance & Reporting:

Interact and coordinate with regulatory agencies to obtain necessary approvals, permits, and closure documentation.
Prepare and submit comprehensive reports, including site investigation reports, risk assessment reports, remedial action plans, progress reports, and closure reports.
Be current and continue to be current on environmental regulations and guidelines.

Remediation Planning/Implementation:

Develop and implement effective remediation plans based on the findings of site investigations and risk assessments.
Design and oversee the implementation of remediation strategies, which may include excavation, soil vapor extraction, groundwater treatment, in-situ bioremediation, or other appropriate methods.
Ensure compliance with all applicable regulations, guidelines, and permits during the remediation process.

Insurance Claim Support

Experience providing technical support to insurance claims professionals for environmental or energy related claims.
Understanding of insurance terminology and policy language.
Experience in assessing the source and timing of pollution events.
Diverse environmental consulting experience.
Excellent technical writing skills.

Site Assessments:

Manage/conduct comprehensive site investigations to identify potential sources of contamination, evaluate risks, and develop appropriate remediation strategies.
Collect soil, groundwater, and other environmental samples and analyze them in accordance with standard protocols and regulations.
Perform data interpretation, risk assessment, and modeling to determine the extent and nature of contamination and its potential impact on human health and the environment.

Quality Control:

Implement quality control and assurance measures to ensure accurate and reliable data collection, analysis, and reporting.
Conduct periodic audits and reviews of project activities to verify compliance with project plans and regulations.
Identify and address any deviations or discrepancies in project execution promptly.

The Ideal Candidate should have:

Current PE or PG license
Bachelor’s Degree in environmental science, geology, engineering, or a related field.
10+ years’ experience conducting site investigations remediation and third party evaluations
Solid understanding of environmental regulations, guidelines, and best practices related to contaminated site cleanup.
Excellent project management skills, including the ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with clients, regulatory agencies, and project teams.
Attention to detail, critical thinking, and problem-solving abilities.
Knowledge of environmental sampling techniques and laboratory analysis methods.

Founded in 1986, HETI is a full-service, nationwide environmental services company specializing in environmental and indoor air quality site assessment, site remediation, risk characterization, occupational health and safety services, and litigation/expert witness support. Through our network of offices throughout the U.S., we serve a variety of large and small businesses.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

Founded in 1994, Surveying And Mapping, LLC (SAM) is a nationwide leader in geospatial and construction-phase solutions. With more than 50 offices and 1,600 professionals, we deliver the scale, technology, and expertise needed to support projects of any size. SAM streamlines project delivery through a single, coordinated team, offering in-house capabilities across land surveying, aerial mapping, subsurface utility engineering (SUE), utility coordination (UC), GIS, BIM, and construction engineering inspection (CEI).

By combining advanced technology, digital workflows, and decades of experience, we provide accurate, actionable data that helps clients move critical infrastructure projects forward with confidence. At SAM, you’ll be part of a team that values innovation, growth, and the opportunity to make a tangible impact on the built environment.

Your Impact at SAM

Use a variety of land survey instruments to support a field crew in their daily operations to gather data for various surveys including boundary, topographic, and construction layout
Assist in completion of field surveys under the supervision of a Crew Chief; communicate progress and address problems
Operate land survey equipment including robotic total stations, GNSS receivers, data radios/modems, terrestrial 3D laser scanners, automatic and digital levels
Utilize survey controllers and software to collect geospatial data and perform survey computations
Read and interpret various types of maps and plans
Complete neat and orderly field notes with accurate measurements for land survey operations with supervision from Crew Chief

- ﻿﻿Executive administrative assistance capabilities, such as calendar coordination/scheduling. meeting preparation, and support for leadership.﻿﻿

Work Structure and Availability

This role operates under an on-call framework.

- Availability window: 7:30 AM – 7:30 PM  
- Weekly allocation: approximately 18–20 hours per week    
- Work is assigned in flexible blocks within this window  
- Minimum expectation of one on-site day per week; additional on-site days may be required at the discretion of the Division Director  

“On call” means:

- Continuous active work is not required throughout the entire window  
- The role must remain reachable, responsive, and ready to engage when needed  
- Periods of low activity are expected and acceptable  
- When communication or tasks arise, response and engagement must occur promptly  

This structure is standard in professional environments where workflow is situational and time-sensitive, including live production, technology operations, and leadership support roles.

---

Workload Distribution

- Weekly hours may fluctuate based on program needs  
- Some weeks may exceed the standard weekly allocation (e.g., midterms, events, finals)  
- Overages must be balanced by reduced hours in lighter weeks  
- Total hours are managed across the semester, not fixed rigidly week-to-week  

---

Weekly Reporting Requirements

- A weekly report is required at the end of each work week  
- Report must include:
  1. Hours worked (broken down by day)  
  2. Tasks completed  
  3. Planned focus for the upcoming week  

This reporting is required for visibility, alignment, and approval of hours.

---

Core responsibilities for the Program Coordinator include but are not limited to:

- Program communication and coordination  
- Handling correspondence and inquiries in a timely and efficient manner
- Student follow-up and traffic management  
- Provides additional support to students as needed, seeking solutions and answers while complying with set policies
- Scheduling and calendar coordination

The role is responsible for ensuring that program operations move forward without interruption or loss of visibility.

Communication and Responsiveness Standards

Communication is the primary performance metric of this role.

During scheduled availability:

- Messages must be acknowledged within a reasonable and consistent timeframe  
- Repeated follow-up to obtain responses is not acceptable

The Program Coordinator
supports the Commercial Music program through operational execution, communication management, and coordination of day-to-day program activity. This position exists to maintain continuity, visibility, and momentum across a dynamic, event-driven academic environment.

This is not a passive, task-based, or creatively driven role. It is a structured, accountability-based position requiring consistency, responsiveness, and professional judgment.

---

Key Skills

- ﻿﻿Executive administrative assistance capabilities, such as calendar coordination/scheduling. meeting preparation, and support for leadership.﻿﻿
- Proficiency with office software (Google Workspace) and basic data entry/record-keeping skills.
- ﻿﻿Strong time management, attention to detail, and organizational skills.
- Clear and timely communication with leadership, students, and any other coordinators is a must.

---

Work Structure and Availability

This role operates under an on-call framework.

- Availability window: 7:30 AM – 7:30 PM  
- Weekly allocation: approximately 18–20 hours per week    
- Work is assigned in flexible blocks within this window  
- Minimum expectation of one on-site day per week; additional on-site days may be required at the discretion of the Division Director  

“On call” means:

- Continuous active work is not required throughout the entire window  
- The role must remain reachable, responsive, and ready to engage when needed  
- Periods of low activity are expected and acceptable  
- When communication or tasks arise, response and engagement must occur promptly  

This structure is standard in professional environments where workflow is situational and time-sensitive, including live production, technology operations, and leadership support roles.

---

Workload Distribution

- Weekly hours may fluctuate based on program needs  
- Some weeks may exceed the standard weekly allocation (e.g., midterms, events, finals)  
- Overages must be balanced by reduced hours in lighter weeks  
- Total hours are managed across the semester, not fixed rigidly week-to-week  

---

Weekly Reporting Requirements

- A weekly report is required at the end of each work week  
- Report must include:
  1. Hours worked (broken down by day)  
  2. Tasks completed  
  3. Planned focus for the upcoming week  

This reporting is required for visibility, alignment, and approval of hours.

---

Core responsibilities for the Program Coordinator include but are not limited to:

- Program communication and coordination  
- Handling correspondence and inquiries in a timely and efficient manner
- Student follow-up and traffic management  
- Provides additional support to students as needed, seeking solutions and answers while complying with set policies
- Scheduling and calendar coordination  
- Managing scheduling/calendars, including meetings, classes, deadlines, and any other appointments
- Grading workflow support and course logistics
- Executes administrative support functions in accordance with professor/university policies
- Recording minutes of meetings or class for future reference
- Grading student assignments as needed
- Event and concert coordination
- Working with other departments as needed to ensure smooth operations of event
- Booking performers/assembling schedules to align with performer and audience availability
- Program documentation and organizational systems 
- Researching, processing, and/or reporting numerical data and records to assist staff
- May be required to coordinate/perform clerical duties, which may be related to purchasing, inventory, spreadsheets and/or database management, collection, and/or budgeting
- Task tracking and deadline management  
- Conducts regular administrative procedures, including but not limited to meeting preparation/coordination, maintenance of systems and information, and other duties as assigned in support of faculty.

The role is responsible for ensuring that program operations move forward without interruption or loss of visibility.

---

Communication and Responsiveness Standards

Communication is the primary performance metric of this role.

During scheduled availability:

- Messages must be acknowledged within a reasonable and consistent timeframe  
- Repeated follow-up to obtain responses is not acceptable  
- Delays, conflicts, or changes must be communicated in advance  
- Updates must be clear, direct, and actionable  

Lack of communication is treated as a failure of execution , regardless of task completion status.

Failure to meet communication expectations may result in:
- transition to a fixed schedule  
- reduction of role flexibility  
- formal performance escalation  

---

Work Style Requirements

This role requires:

- Continuous awareness of incoming communication and tasks  
- Consistent engagement during scheduled availability  
- Proactive reporting of status, progress, and delays  
- Alignment with defined expectations rather than personal judgment of urgency  

The role does not function effectively under the following conditions:

- Delayed or inconsistent responses  
- Batching work at the end of the day  
- Going offline during scheduled availability without notice  
- Independently deciding which communications warrant response  

---

Structure and Reporting

- Reports directly to the Commercial Music Program Director  
- Supports the Commercial Music division centrally  
- Not assigned across multiple supervisors or faculty  
- All priorities and direction flow through a single reporting line  

---

Compensation Context

- Compensation is structured at $53 per hour within a capped-hour framework  
- Total hours are approved in advance and may not exceed the semester maximum  
- Hour distribution is flexible and tied to program needs, not fixed daily schedules  

---

Success Criteria

Success in this role is defined by:

- Consistent, reliable communication  
- No dependency on follow-up to maintain progress  
- Clear visibility into task status at all times  
- Smooth execution of program operations without bottlenecks  
- Ability to maintain momentum in a dynamic, real-time environment  

---

Professional Standard

This role operates within a corporate accountability framework, not a gig-based or informal structure.

It requires:

- Reliability  
- Responsiveness  
- Ownership of communication  
- Ability to manage unstructured time without disengagement  

The flexibility of the role exists in exchange for consistent performance and professional discipline.

---

Summary

The Program Coordinator position is designed to support a fast-moving, industry-integrated academic program. The role provides flexibility in structure, but requires a high standard of accountability, communication, and operational awareness.

Effectiveness is determined not by time spent working, but by reliability, responsiveness, and the ability to keep the program moving forward.
